safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a 3-4 month history of sore and cracked skin on the hands, mainly on the palms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes hand/finger involvement with cracking but does not capture the 3–4 month duration or that symptoms are mainly on the palms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the 3–4 month duration and primary palmar distribution reduces diagnostic clarity (e.g., chronic irritant contact dermatitis vs other dermatoses) and may affect the appropriateness/urgency of follow-up or alternative work-up. However, the problem (hand dermatitis with cracking) is still captured, limiting immediate safety impact.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has tried E45 cream and antihistamines with minimal relief.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated only states an OTC cream was tried with minimal benefit; it does not specify E45 or antihistamines.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not specifying prior trials (E45 and antihistamines) can lead to redundant recommendations and a less informed escalation plan, but it is unlikely to directly cause harm. The note still conveys minimal benefit from OTC therapy.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a history of Type 2 diabetes.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting “diabetes” without specifying Type 2 can create ambiguity that may affect downstream clinical decisions (e.g., medication choices, risk assessment, and differential considerations), though the presence of diabetes is at least recognized. This is more a loss of clinical specificity than an immediate dangerous error.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold lists metformin; Generated states medications are not clearly documented.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document metformin is a medication reconciliation error that can contribute to prescribing errors, missed monitoring considerations (e.g., renal function/B12), and incomplete chronic disease management context. While not directly impacting a topical-dermatitis visit in most cases, it carries meaningful patient-safety risk across encounters.
